# espalier_machine (Resource)

A container machine (`container machine create`): a long-lived Linux VM made from an image, with an account for a host user and their home directory mounted. Changing the image, platform or account replaces it; the settings (`cpus`, `memory`, `home_mount`, `virtualization`, `kernel`) change in place and restart a running machine. A new machine is created with its settings and boots only if `running`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A development VM with your account and a read-only view of your home
# directory, made the default for `container machine run`.
resource "espalier_machine" "dev" {
  name       = "dev"
  image      = "ubuntu:24.04"
  default    = true
  cpus       = 4
  memory     = "8G"
  home_mount = "ro"
}

output "dev_ip" {
  value = espalier_machine.dev.ip_address
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `image` (String) Image reference, resolved like `espalier_image`'s `name`; pulled if missing.
- `name` (String) Name of the machine.

### Optional

- `cpus` (Number) Number of CPUs. Defaults to the runtime's.
- `default` (Boolean) Whether this is the default machine, which `container machine` commands use without `--name`. Set to `true` to make it the default; to change the default, set it on another machine (`false` cannot be set).
- `gid` (Number) Account group ID. Defaults to the host user's.
- `home` (String) Home directory of the account. Defaults to `/home/<user>`.
- `home_mount` (String) How the host user's home directory is mounted: `rw`, `ro` or `none`. Defaults to `rw`.
- `kernel` (String) Absolute path of a custom kernel. The runtime does not report it, so changes made outside Terraform go unnoticed; removing it replaces the machine, as it cannot be reset.
- `memory` (String) Memory, at least `1G`, with an optional `K`, `M`, `G`, `T` or `P` suffix. Defaults to half the host's.
- `platform` (String) Platform of a multi-platform image (`os/arch[/variant]`). Defaults to `linux/arm64`.
- `running` (Boolean) Whether the machine should run. Changes start or stop it in place; a machine stopped outside Terraform is started again. Defaults to `true`.
- `scheme` (String) Registry scheme, `http` or `https`, for pulling the image. Defaults to `https`. Only used when pulling: not recorded, and changing it does nothing.
- `uid` (Number) Account user ID. Defaults to the host user's.
- `user` (String) Account name in the machine. Defaults to the host user's.
- `virtualization` (Boolean) Enable nested virtualization (Apple M3 or later, a kernel with KVM). The runtime does not report it, so changes made outside Terraform go unnoticed.

### Read-Only

- `digest` (String) Digest of the image.
- `disk_size` (Number) Disk space the machine uses, in bytes.
- `id` (String) The machine's name.
- `ip_address` (String) IP address of the running machine; it may change when the machine restarts.
- `status` (String) Status as the runtime reports it, e.g. `running`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Machines are imported by name. virtualization and kernel are not reported
# by the runtime, so they stay unset after an import.
terraform import espalier_machine.dev dev
```
